anatomy.flutter: Select<T>(options, value, onChanged, placeholder, size, enabled, disabledReason, invalid, expand, width, focusNode, label, hint) internally composes the trigger (Surface+Row+chevron Icon) and, on open, an OverlayEntry running SelectMenu<T> (public per ruling L6) over PopoverSurface with SelectChild variants SelectOption/SelectGroup/SelectSeparator flattened by _MenuGeometry into _Row rows (_SelectItem/_SelectLabel/_SelectSeparator) plus conditional _ScrollButton caps.
anatomy.web: select.tsx exports all ten pieces the Dart file's header table enumerates as ported: Select, SelectGroup, SelectValue, SelectTrigger, SelectContent (Portal+ScrollUpButton+Viewport+ScrollDownButton), SelectLabel, SelectItem, SelectSeparator, SelectScrollUpButton, SelectScrollDownButton, each a thin data-slot wrapper over SelectPrimitive.* from radix-ui.

api.flutter: SelectOption<T>(value, label, enabled, disabledReason) and Select<T>(..., disabledReason, ...) both carry 'Why the row/trigger is disabled. Shown as a tooltip while [enabled] is false' with the item falling back to nothing and the trigger falling back to the enclosing FieldScope's; SelectSize is a 2-member enum (sm/md) matching data-size sm/default.
api.web: CLOSED: SelectTrigger and SelectItem now take disabledReason?: string (components/ui/select.tsx). SelectTrigger wraps in components/ui/disabled.tsx's Disabled in native mode (Radix's Select.Trigger is a real <button disabled>); SelectItem wraps in aria mode (Radix's Select.Item is a role="option" div with no native disabled attribute). Both add an always-on aria-describedby plus a click/tap-reachable popover. ORIGINAL: SelectTrigger takes size?: "sm" | "default" (matching Flutter's 2 rungs) and forwards disabled straight from Radix with no reason/explanation prop; the doc's API Reference lists only 'disabled: boolean, native Radix prop' for the trigger and 'value (required), disabled' for SelectItem, with no explanatory-text mechanism anywhere in select.tsx.
api.note: CLOSED 2026-09-11: measured in the dev server (http://localhost:3111, desktop-dark) — focusing a disabled trigger or item with disabledReason set reads the reason via aria-describedby; the info button opens a Popover on click/Enter/Space. Pinned by test/select.test.tsx and e2e/gaps-disabled.spec.ts. ORIGINAL: Same disabledReason gap seen on radio/checkbox/questionnaire in this system: Flutter's tooltip explanation for a disabled trigger or option has no web counterpart — a disabled web select only communicates 'you cannot use this,' never why, with no FieldScope-style fallback either.

states.flutter: _triggerFill/_triggerBorder/_triggerRing compute rest/hover/focus/open/invalid colours, explicitly noting 'the only hover state any control on this page authors, and it exists in one theme' (dark: theme.input at 30%/50% via _darkFillAlpha/_darkHoverFillAlpha) — the class doc calls this DOCUMENTED DRIFT (forms-map drift 17, selects-map drift 19).
states.web: SelectTrigger's className carries the identical asymmetric rule: `dark:bg-input/30 dark:hover:bg-input/50` with no light-mode hover class at all, plus `focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50` and `aria-invalid:border-destructive aria-invalid:ring-3 aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20`; SelectItem highlight is `focus:bg-accent focus:text-accent-foreground`, matching Flutter's 'Radix moves DOM focus onto the highlighted item, so :focus is the highlight' comment on _SelectItem.

disabled.flutter: Select wraps the trigger in Disabled(disabled: !_fieldEnabled, reason: widget.disabledReason ?? _scope?.disabledReason); the class doc records DOCUMENTED PARITY (ruling L5): an empty SelectContent renders behind a trigger that cannot open it, because _openMenu early-returns on `_menu.options.isEmpty`, 'which is the reference's own answer, reached from the other side.'
disabled.web: CLOSED: see the api dimension above — disabledReason is now present on both SelectTrigger and SelectItem, wired through components/ui/disabled.tsx. The empty-menu behaviour this dimension already recorded as matched is unchanged. ORIGINAL: SelectTrigger's disabled styling is `disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50` with no reason text; the doc's own 'disabled' StateCell renders `<Select disabled><SelectTrigger aria-label="Disabled">` with nothing explaining why, and the Keyboard section confirms 'During disabled: Removed from the tab sequence entirely' matching Flutter's IgnorePointer/Focus(canRequestFocus:false) treatment.
disabled.note: CLOSED 2026-09-11: same fix and evidence as the api dimension; the empty-menu parity already noted stands unchanged. ORIGINAL: The empty-menu behaviour is genuinely matched (both sides independently prevent opening a menu with nothing selectable), but the reason/tooltip explanation Flutter attaches to a disabled trigger or item has no web equivalent, which is the same disabledReason gap recorded under api.

interaction.flutter: _onTriggerKey opens on Enter/NumpadEnter/Space/ArrowDown/ArrowUp; _onMenuKey handles ArrowDown/ArrowUp (_move, wrapping to the next enabled row), Home/End (walk to an edge then _move), Enter/Space (_commit), and Escape/Tab (_closeMenu) — there is no letter/typeahead handling anywhere in the switch.
interaction.web: select/page.tsx's Keyboard section documents the identical Enter/Space/ArrowDown-opens, Arrow-navigates, Enter/Space-commits, Escape-closes-without-changing, Tab-closes-and-advances-focus set, plus one Flutter does not have: 'Typing a letter — Typeahead — jumps to the next item whose label starts with what was typed,' explicitly because 'Radix Select implements the ARIA listbox pattern, including typeahead.'
interaction.note: Every keyboard path Flutter implements matches the web's documented behaviour exactly; the one difference is additive on the web side — Radix's built-in typeahead has no equivalent in _SelectState._onMenuKey — so this is not a web gap, but worth flagging since a reader might assume typeahead is ported when it is not.

semantics.flutter: The trigger is Semantics(button: true, label, hint, value: chosen?.label ?? placeholder, expanded: _open, enabled: _enabled); each _SelectItem is Semantics(button: true, selected: checked, enabled: option.enabled, label: option.label); _SelectLabel and SelectGroup's grouping carry no Semantics node of their own at all — they are plain Padding+StyledText.
semantics.web: The doc's Accessibility section states 'Trigger role: combobox, with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the content,' 'Content role: listbox, with each SelectItem exposed as role option and aria-selected on the current value,' and 'Groups: SelectGroup renders role group, labelled by its SelectLabel via aria-labelledby' — the full ARIA listbox/combobox/group pattern via Radix.
semantics.note: The web achieves a richer, standards-mapped ARIA role set (combobox/listbox/option/group with aria-labelledby) via Radix, while Flutter approximates the same information with generic button/selected/expanded Semantics flags and has no group-to-label association at all; this is the web exceeding Flutter's semantics rather than falling short of them.
